To which principal rite can we call the vasordhārā performed with the camaka mantras an "upahoma"? There is no principal homa there at all. Are these two upahomas of two forms of the camaka mantras?
13. The Rudra homa is not one of the original pākasaṃsthās, is it! Among the original seven pākayajña saṃsthās enjoined by Baudhāyana, such as aupāsana, vaiśvadeva, sthālīpāka, aṣṭakā..... and so on, this "Rudra homa" of the namaka and camaka does not occur at all, does it. Rather than applying the general rules of the upahoma of the pākasaṃsthās — the source of vasordhārā, which comes from agnicayana, a haviḥsaṃsthā of the śrauta, lies in the śrauta "agnicayana" sacrifice. There, vasordhārā is poured unbroken only at the concluding stage, when the oblations to all the deities, the sviṣṭakṛt and the prāyaścitta are all finished and the sacrifice is complete. When applying the śrauta basis to the smārta Rudra homa (when performing atideśa), one must adopt its original position, "the end of the entire homa", and not the place of the sviṣṭakṛt in the middle.
14. Where one says pādādikeśānta (from the feet to the end of the hair), does keśānta mean the root of the hair or the tip of the hair?? Thus it is said "ante vasordhārā ca" (and at the end, the vasordhārā); nowhere is it written "pradhānānte vasordhārā" (vasordhārā at the end of the principal [homa]) or "sviṣṭakṛdaṅgatvena vasordhārā" (vasordhārā as an aṅga of the sviṣṭakṛt). Therefore it is just to take the word "anta" that occurs here as meaning "the end of the entire homa" (the proximity of the pūrṇāhuti).
15. In the Ekādaśa Rudra homa (complete homa) of the threefold-division option:
tredhāvibhāgapakṣāśrayaṇena tisra āhutayaḥ. tataś camakānuvākair vasordhārā ca. sampūrṇahomapakṣe pratirūpakaṃ tisras tisra āhutaya iti trayastriṃśat. rūpakānte rūpakānte ekaikena camakavibhāgenaikaikā āhutir ekādaśa pūrvābhiḥ saha catuścatvāriṃśat. ante vasordhārā ca
(Adopting the option of the threefold division, three oblations; then the vasordhārā with the camaka anuvākas. In the option of the complete homa, three oblations for each rūpaka, making thirty-three; at the end of each rūpaka, one oblation with one division of the camaka, eleven, which together with the previous ones make forty-four; and at the end, the vasordhārā.)
There is this statement. If, on the basis of this statement, one argues that vasordhārā is merely an aṅga within the sviṣṭakṛt, the calculation of the total number of oblations given here becomes wrong. Some say there is a tradition of including the vasordhārā homa in the anvādhāna. How is it possible here to perform the anvādhāna declaring vasordhārā as a principal homa or as an upahoma? According to the rule of anvādhāna, one must clearly mention to which deity and with which substance the homa is performed, e.g. the principal deity, the subsidiary deities. If the camaka vasordhārā were merely an upahoma in the middle, its numerical reckoning should have been completed along with the principal. But since the reckoning of the text keeps vasordhārā outside the count, there is a contradiction with the arithmetic in making a saṅkalpa for it as an "upahoma" in the anvādhāna. It is neither an upahoma nor a principal homa.
16. Does not the singular word "vasordhārā ca" indicate, not merely an oblation of a sruva-ful, but a single unbroken oblation poured without interruption throughout the recitation of the 11 anuvākas of the camaka?
17. Giving oblations with the camaka mantras separately, up to 44 oblations, is the "Śatarudrīya aṅga homa". After that, the rule separated off by the word "ca", proclaiming in the singular an unbroken oblation, is the "vasordhārā". It is precisely because it is an unbroken principle that does not enter into the count that it has been kept outside the arithmetical list of 44.
18. The chief characteristic of an upahoma is "being manifestive of the principal rite" (pradhānakarmavyañjakatva). "ante vasordhārā ca" is enjoined only after the count of the 44 Śatarudrīya oblations is finished. By the time the vasordhārā takes place, the principal namaka oblations are over. When the principal rite itself is not present there, whom can the vasordhārā "manifest"? Can the characteristic of being an upahoma stand where there is no principal?
19. The basic characteristic of vasordhārā is "avicchinnāṃ ghṛtadhārām" (an unbroken stream of ghee); is not "upahoma" the characteristic of a rite poured in separate oblations? By the rule "ekasya ubhayatve saṃyogapṛthaktvam" (when one thing serves two purposes, it is through distinct connections), in a single prayoga the same characteristic "upahoma" cannot be applied twice, at two different places, to the same group of mantras (the camaka).
Once the camaka oblations made separately along with the namaka (the 11 camaka oblations) have been called "upahoma", the vasordhārā that comes after them cannot also be called "upahoma". If it is called so, it becomes the fault of repetition (punarukti) and of confusion of characteristics (lakṣaṇasaṅkara).
20. Since vasordhārā has been kept outside that count, one cannot make a saṅkalpa for it as merely another "upahoma". It is an independent rite in the form of "yāga samṛddhi" (fullness of the sacrifice), which brings the fruit of the entire sacrifice, and not an upahoma.
**Summary**
1. In the statements of the sages, the sūtras, the smṛtis and the Purāṇas that are authoritative for the smārta Rudra homa, vasordhārā is not stated as an aṅga of the Rudra homa. It is not stated even together with the pūrṇāhuti. If vasordhārā is not performed, there is no deficiency whatsoever.
Many reasons have been given why vasordhārā cannot be included among the upahomas, before the sviṣṭakṛt, as an aṅga of the Rudra homa. The opinions of many scholars have also been given.
2. It may be said that, understanding "ante" in the Madanamahārṇava or in the Māndhātṛ Karmavipāka to mean "at the end of the camaka", many in Tamil Nadu and Kerala have been performing vasordhārā before the sviṣṭakṛt, and that it gradually became customary. Once it became customary, things like śivatanuprīṇana, upahoma, and having to include it in the anvādhāna saṅkalpa were all used to justify it. But in the Mahārṇava, vasordhārā is not counted in the number of oblations of the principal Rudra homa; it is kept outside. In the Rudra homa rule itself, along with the camaka anuvākas, the Āgneya sūkta, Viṣṇu sūkta, Rudra sūkta, Aindava sūkta, Vaiśvānara sāman and Jyeṣṭha sāmans are also prescribed for the vasordhārā; after the vasordhārā with the camakas is finished among the upahomas, it is in any case impossible to perform a vasordhārā homa with the various other sūktas. Moreover, in the navagraha śānti, vasordhārā is stated after the pūrṇāhuti, and they have explained that it is performed for the desire of an abundance of fruit. In the Karmavipāka Mahārṇava and in the Māndhātṛ Karmavipāka, "ante" must be understood as meaning "pūrṇāhutyante" (at the end of the pūrṇāhuti). It is clear that vasordhārā is stated in relation to Agni, not as an aṅga of the Rudra homa.
3. In the one-tenth and one-hundredth Rudra homas, performing one tenth for the remaining rūpakas, and the rule of vasordhārā after the pūrṇāhuti, have been prescribed by the authors of the digests in accordance with the principles of Mīmāṃsā. It becomes clear that they prescribed it only after the pūrṇāhuti for these reasons: because in the śrauta all the procedures of agnicayana are done in relation to the deity Agni; because vasordhārā too is itself an abhiṣeka performed for Agni; because Agni is also one of the deities of the camakas; because the vasordhārā stated in the Matsya Purāṇa is likewise stated after the pūrṇāhuti, in relation to Agni, with the Āgneya and other sūktas; because, whatever the principal deity may be, the pūrṇāhuti in the gṛhya is performed for the pleasure of the deity Agni; and because the principles of Mīmāṃsā also apply. They did not include it among the upahomas as an aṅga of the Rudra homa against the statements of the sages, the smṛtis, the Purāṇas, the sūtras and Sāyaṇa's commentary. In sum, if vasordhārā is to be performed in the Rudra homa, performing it after the pūrṇāhuti is the appropriate and śāstric course.
